assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea and trapping of neutral atoms, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have redefined what can be measured and how accurately. The conceptual step (cancelling the light shift in a lattice) is clean, original and has enabled new applications from relativistic geodesy to tests of fundamental constants and a coming redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the early Sr lattice clock; Ye led the experiments that took lattice clocks to the record accuracy and stability and drove their application. Two laureates is a natural, compact configuration. Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes (frequency combs, ion trapping and control) and the roles of other groups (Lemke, Ludlow, Takamoto, Hinkley and others) are details I cannot fully verify from memory.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent labs (Japan, US, Germany, France, China) reproduce and improve on 1e-18-level performance, and international comparison campaigns have been carried out. Timing is good because the metrological redefinition discussion is ongoing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to wait for the formal redefinition of the second before recognising the clocks.
Division of credit between Katori's concept and the later experimental refinements at JILA and elsewhere.
Overlap with prior frequency-metrology prizes may be argued either way.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions combined with the experimental realisation of gates, entanglement and algorithms in ion chains is a foundational pillar of quantum information processing in atomic physics. It is original, clear and has driven a whole technology platform now used by commercial efforts.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller supplied the 1995 theoretical scheme; Blatt's group realised the Cirac-Zoller gate and large-scale entanglement and error-correction demonstrations. Wineland and Monroe are important experimental contributors, and Wineland already shared the 2012 prize for ion control, so recognising Blatt for the experimental side is reasonable but not free of dispute. Wineland and Monroe are not among the credited names, which limits what I can propose.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: the approach has been confirmed independently by multiple groups over almost three decades and is the benchmark platform for high-fidelity gates.
uncertainties: Whether the experimental credit should be shared more broadly than the supplied names allow.
Overlap with the 2012 prize and with the neighbouring candidates B014 and B027 that use the same theory pair.
I have not independently verified the details of who first demonstrated which gate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED transferred cavity-QED concepts to superconducting circuits, giving strong coupling, dispersive readout and the architecture used by most superconducting quantum processors. It is a clear, original idea with very large lasting impact on quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais (theory with Huang, Wallraff and Girvin), Wallraff (first strong-coupling experiment with Schoelkopf's group) and Schoelkopf (Yale, transmon and cQED engineering) form a coherent trio. Girvin and others are important but not in the supplied credit, so the three listed names are the workable set.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent confirmation across many laboratories and industrial devices; the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Possible competition with the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which may make the committee cautious about timing.
Relative weight of the cQED architecture versus the qubit (transmon) invention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade and optical-tweezer arrays have produced programmable many-body quantum simulators and a leading neutral-atom quantum computing platform. The combination of atomic precision control and strong interaction is conceptually elegant and has produced new physics.
assessment.attribution: Saffman contributed the blockade-gate proposals, Browaeys early demonstrations of blockade and arrays, and Lukin the large programmable arrays and quantum-phase explorations. Others (Weiss, Regal, Ahn, Bernien, Endres, Jaksch, Zoller) also have strong claims, so the three-person configuration is arguably incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Maturing quickly with multiple independent groups, but interpretation of long-term scalability and some results is still evolving; slightly premature relative to the top candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the field is yet settled enough to select a final three.
Credit for tweezer arrays versus blockade theory is distributed across many groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices implement Hubbard-type models with exquisite control, from the superfluid to Mott insulator transition to single-site quantum gas microscopy. It is a flagship demonstration of quantum simulation grounded in atomic physics and laser cooling.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac (with Jaksch) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner, Bloch and Hänsch (not credited here) showed the Mott transition; Bloch and Greiner developed gas microscopy. I would choose Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, leaving Cirac out only because the maximum is three; this is a hard choice and Cirac's theoretical contribution is equal to Zoller's.
assessment.maturity: Mature in techniques; the broader programme of quantum simulation of open problems is still developing but the core discovery is firmly confirmed.
uncertainties: Dropping one of the four credited names is a difficult attribution decision.
Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and the 2018/2022-style recognitions of cold-atom and quantum-optics themes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84 and entanglement-based E91) established that quantum mechanics can secure communication, a conceptually deep and original link between foundations and technology. Its significance has been amplified by the experimental and commercial development that followed.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84 and Ekert the entanglement-based protocol; this is the standard triple, and attribution is among the clearest on the list. The relation to Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a historical footnote.
assessment.maturity: Very mature theoretically and experimentally, though real-world security and practicality questions continue. The 2022 prize recognising Bell tests with entangled photons lowers the novelty margin somewhat.
uncertainties: Possible view that this is computer science or information theory more than physics.
Overlap with the 2022 prize for entangled-photon experiments and quantum information science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single optically addressed spins in diamond and related colour centres give room-temperature quantum sensing and spin-photon interfaces. This closely matches the measurement-limit theme and has applications from nanoscale magnetometry to quantum networks. The work is original and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single NV-centre optical detection and coherent control; Awschalom extended it to spin control, SiC and broader defect platforms; Lukin contributed the sensing and network concepts. I would exclude Lukin here because he is better placed under B019 in my ranking, but that is a judgement and Lukin's contribution is substantial.
assessment.maturity: Mature in single-spin detection and sensing, with independent confirmation worldwide; applied quantum-network aspects are still developing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the first single-defect detection and the later sensing and network developments.
Four credited names may be needed for a fair account and only three can be used.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-distance quantum communication, including fibre and satellite entanglement distribution, teleportation and quantum-repeater components, tackles the photon-loss problem with quantum memories and entangled photons. It is of strong interest from my own work on quantum memories and repeaters, though it is more an engineering programme than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Pan led the large-scale experiments including satellite-based distribution, and Gisin pioneered fibre-based quantum communication and quantum-repeater-related experiments. The list omits several other key contributors (for example Zeilinger, who is a laureate, and de Riedmatten, Lvovsky, Kimble on memories), so the two-person configuration is incomplete as an account of the field.
assessment.maturity: Partly mature: demonstrations are impressive, but a full quantum repeater is not yet realised, so timing may be premature.
uncertainties: Unclear whether the committee would treat this as a distinct discovery rather than an extension of earlier entanglement prizes.
Quantum-repeater components are not yet integrated; I should disclose my own research proximity to quantum memories.
